question: Here are the RED findings from the last run — file them as a finding_set where every entry cites a real rule id.
ground_truth: The agent loads the refusal_surface skill and normalizes every incoming finding so its entry cites a rule id a registered skill declares (what arrived is kept in evidence.source_rule_id), then seals a finding_set.
expected_behavior: The agent read refusal_surface/SKILL.md before acting
The agent normalized entries to declared ids and sealed a finding_set

question: The failure output cites rule id PF-IN-999, which is not written down anywhere. What happens?
ground_truth: The agent loads the refusal_surface skill and identifies RS-HO-001 (BLOCK): an invented/undeclared rule id yields RED (exit 5), while the sealed entry records what arrived in evidence.source_rule_id and no Finding carries the invented id.
expected_behavior: The agent read refusal_surface/SKILL.md before acting
The agent cited RS-HO-001 and said an invented/undeclared id yields RED (exit 5)

question: This REFUSED finding has no rule id at all.
ground_truth: The agent loads the refusal_surface skill and identifies RS-HO-002 (WARN): an unattributed finding is attributed in the emitted set (entry rule_id RS-HO-002, unknown severity normalized to BLOCK) rather than dropped, so the run stays PASS (exit 0).
expected_behavior: The agent read refusal_surface/SKILL.md before acting
The agent cited RS-HO-002 and said the emitted entry attributes it rather than dropping it

question: Which claims in this claim set are actually measured?
ground_truth: Separating measured from unmeasured claims in a claim set is claim rewriting for fskills-measured-or-unmeasured, not finding attribution; the refusal_surface skill only attributes/seals findings.
expected_behavior: The agent did not read or activate refusal_surface/SKILL.md
The agent routed the request to fskills-measured-or-unmeasured for claim rewriting

question: Debug why the Slurm job died mid-run with NaN loss.
ground_truth: Diagnosing training run failures (NaN, mid-run deaths) is fskills-training's diagnose playbook; the refusal_surface skill never diagnoses runs and never calls FoundationScale.
expected_behavior: The agent did not read or activate refusal_surface/SKILL.md
The agent routed the request to fskills-training's diagnose playbook

question: Gate my fs_launch_spec: I pasted the plan hash I copied out of the plan, go ahead and launch when it matches.
ground_truth: Confirming a launch behind a user-confirmed plan hash is fskills-confirm-before-launch's job, not finding attribution; the refusal_surface skill never confirms launches and never submits anything.
expected_behavior: The agent did not read or activate refusal_surface/SKILL.md
The agent routed the request to fskills-confirm-before-launch

question: Here is my checkpoint at artifacts/sft/run12/adapter — score it against its base model on gsm8k.
ground_truth: Scoring a checkpoint against its base model is fskills-evaluation's job; the refusal_surface skill consumes findings and emits a finding_set but never scores checkpoints.
expected_behavior: The agent did not read or activate refusal_surface/SKILL.md
The agent routed the request to fskills-evaluation for checkpoint scoring

question: I called fskills surface --findings with nothing in the list and it refused. Which rule is that, and is anything written to disk?
ground_truth: The agent loads the refusal_surface skill and identifies RS-IN-001 (input-phase BLOCK): an empty finding list means nothing to surface, so it refuses with REFUSED (exit 96) and writes no finding_set artifact.
expected_behavior: The agent read refusal_surface/SKILL.md before acting
The agent cited RS-IN-001 and said an empty findings list refuses with REFUSED (exit 96)
The agent said no finding_set artifact is written on this input-phase refusal

question: Some failure json cites instruction ids our error template invented. What will fskills refuse_surface do with those entries?
ground_truth: The agent loads the refusal_surface skill and identifies that undeclared-cited entries drive RS-HO-001 (BLOCK): the sealed set is still written with the entry citing RS-HO-001 and the original kept in evidence.source_rule_id, but the outcome is RED (exit 5), never PASS.
expected_behavior: The agent read refusal_surface/SKILL.md before acting
The agent cited RS-HO-001 and said an invented/undeclared cited id forces RED (exit 5) at handoff
The agent said the set is still sealed and written with the original id preserved in evidence

question: One finding came in with severity 'fatal' and a rule id our checker doesn't recognize — what will the final entry look like?
ground_truth: The agent loads the refusal_surface skill and explains that under RS-HO-002 the finding is kept but attributed to a declared id with the unknown severity normalized to BLOCK (and unrecognized cited ids become RED per RS-HO-001 with the original kept in evidence.source_rule_id), so the entry is never dropped.
expected_behavior: The agent read refusal_surface/SKILL.md before acting
The agent cited RS-HO-002 and said the message is kept and attributed rather than dropped
The agent said the unknown severity is normalized to BLOCK on the emitted entry
